body:
`owe_reply` applies a 48-hour grace before a thread counts as owed, which is
right for an ordinary comment and wrong for an escalation.

Observed 2026-08-13 on PR #1442. At 17:13Z @chloeroform wrote "Could a human
please step in and take over here? This is getting ridiculous." The board
generated at 18:11Z reported `owe_reply=0`, `never_acked=0`, breaches 0 — a
correct application of the grace, since the comment was under an hour old. A
tick that trusted the zeros would have left that sitting for two days.

The board reads recency and authorship. It has no notion of a comment that is
*asking to be escalated*, so the one signal that should bypass the grace is the
one it cannot see. The grace exists to stop us pestering people mid-conversation;
someone asking for a human is the opposite situation.

This is the third distinct way the board has under-reported a waiting person:
PRs were invisible entirely, F-222645 covered the red-PR half, and now an
escalation inside the grace window. The pattern is that the board models
*elapsed time since our last comment* and not *what was said*.

Suggested shape: a phrase/intent check over comments newer than the grace, which
promotes a thread to `owe_reply` (or a distinct `escalated` section) regardless
of age. Keep it narrow — a request for a human, a statement that the thread is
stuck, an explicit complaint about response time — so it does not become a
sentiment classifier firing on ordinary frustration with the bug itself.

Cost of not fixing it: escalations are exactly the threads where latency is most
expensive, and the grace guarantees we are at worst 48h late on every one.
title: The follow-up board's 48h grace hides an explicit request for a human
